prompt.brief: Design an intelligent capacity-planning platform that forecasts resource demand, models growth and failure scenarios, alerts on saturation risk, and turns recommendations into governed infrastructure decisions.
successSignals: Define resource identity, utilization/availability signals, service dependencies, forecast horizon, scenarios, constraints, confidence, and ownership.
Handle seasonality, growth changes, saturation, reserved capacity, quotas, outages, and uncertainty without presenting estimates as guarantees.
Separate telemetry ingestion from forecasting, simulation, recommendation approval, procurement/workflow execution, and dashboard queries.
Explain feedback, overrides, stale data, multi-cloud costs, auditability, observability, and last-approved-plan fallback.

functional: Collect resource metrics and demand drivers, generate baseline/scenario forecasts, calculate headroom, and flag future capacity risks.
Provide forecasts with intervals, assumptions, cost/options, dependency impact, owner approval, and procurement or scaling recommendations.
Support overrides, what-if simulations, data corrections, forecast versioning, alerts, recommendation execution, and rollback/audit.
nonFunctional: Publish a 90-day forecast with error and uncertainty by resource class and alert before agreed saturation thresholds are reached.
Forecast millions of resource series across clouds without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 5M resource series, 90-day horizons, and 10k service owners
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Intelligent capacity-planning platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Intelligent capacity-planning platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Intelligent capacity-planning platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Intelligent capacity-planning platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Intelligent capacity-planning platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Intelligent capacity-planning platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Intelligent capacity-planning platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Intelligent capacity-planning platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Intelligent capacity-planning platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
